answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks via remote hardware attestation. Agents run inside secure enclaves that sign identities using silicon-fused keys. This forces an attacker to incur the verifiable capital cost of buying physical chips per persona, rendering costless duplication a fable. Trust scales to the zenith of certified silicon, while revoked keys enter a glacier archive. However, this approach centralizes trust in chipmakers and remains vulnerable to side-channel attacks.
